name: Artificial Intelligence
description: Companies involved in AI software, semiconductors, and automation infrastructure.
methodology: Tracked via Global X Robotics & AI ETF (BOTZ). Holdings include companies with significant AI revenue exposure. Limitations: ETF may include robotics firms not purely AI-focused.
overview: AI theme returns are driven by corporate spending on AI infrastructure, semiconductor demand, and software adoption. Returns can be volatile due to hype cycles, regulatory shifts, and rapid technology changes.
risks: 🎯 Sector Concentration: Heavily weighted toward a few mega-cap technology companies
📉 Valuation Risk: High growth expectations already priced in — vulnerable to compression
⚖️ Regulatory Risk: Increasing government scrutiny of AI development and deployment
🔄 Technology Disruption: Rapid innovation can quickly shift competitive advantages
📊 High Volatility: Theme has historically exhibited above-average price swings
limitations: ETF may include robotics firms not purely AI-focused.
whoItsFor: You believe AI will keep growing over the next decade
You're comfortable with big ups and downs
You want exposure to cutting-edge technology
whoItsNotFor: You dislike seeing large drops in value
You prefer companies that pay dividends

name: Clean Energy
description: Solar, wind, battery, and renewable energy infrastructure companies.
methodology: Tracked via iShares Global Clean Energy ETF (ICLN). Covers solar, wind, and other renewable energy companies globally. Limitations: Includes utilities that may have mixed energy sources.
overview: Clean energy returns are influenced by government policy (subsidies, mandates), commodity prices, interest rates (capital-intensive projects), and technological efficiency gains.
risks: ⚖️ Policy Dependence: Returns highly sensitive to government subsidies and regulations
💰 Interest Rate Sensitivity: Capital-intensive sector hurt by rising rates
📉 Cyclical Downturns: Commodity price swings impact profitability
🌍 Geopolitical Risk: Supply chain concentration in specific regions
📊 High Volatility: Historically more volatile than broad market indices
limitations: Includes utilities that may have mixed energy sources.
whoItsFor: You care about sustainability and clean technology
You're a long-term investor (10+ years)
You can handle high ups and downs
whoItsNotFor: You want steady returns year over year
You're uncomfortable with government policy risk
You need income from your investments

name: Semiconductors
description: Chip designers, manufacturers, and semiconductor equipment companies.
methodology: Tracked via VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH). Concentrated portfolio of ~25 major semiconductor companies. Limitations: Top-heavy — top 5 holdings often exceed 40% weight.
overview: Semiconductor returns are driven by cyclical demand patterns, AI infrastructure buildout, consumer electronics, and automotive chip demand. The sector is capital-intensive with long production cycles.
risks: 🔄 Cyclicality: Semiconductor demand follows boom-bust cycles
🌍 Geopolitical Risk: Manufacturing concentrated in Taiwan and South Korea
💰 Capital Intensity: Massive investment required for new fabrication plants
🎯 Customer Concentration: Revenue often dependent on a few large buyers
📊 High Volatility: Amplified market moves due to operating leverage
limitations: Top-heavy — top 5 holdings often exceed 40% weight.
whoItsFor: You want exposure to a critical technology sector
You're OK with boom-and-bust cycles
You have a long time horizon

name: Cybersecurity
description: Network security, cloud security, identity management, and threat detection firms.
methodology: Tracked via First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR). Limitations: Some holdings derive cybersecurity revenue as secondary business line.
overview: Cybersecurity spending is driven by increasing digital threats, regulatory compliance, and enterprise cloud migration. The sector tends to be resilient during downturns as security spending is non-discretionary.
risks: 📉 Valuation Risk: Many cybersecurity firms trade at premium multiples
🔄 Competition: Low barriers create constant competitive pressure
🎯 Acquisition Risk: Smaller firms frequently acquired, changing composition
💰 Profitability Concerns: Many firms prioritize growth over profits
📊 Moderate-High Volatility: Growth stock characteristics amplify market moves
limitations: Some holdings derive cybersecurity revenue as secondary business line.
whoItsFor: You see cybersecurity as a growing necessity
You want tech exposure with some resilience
You're investing for 5+ years

name: Healthcare Innovation
description: Genomics, biotech, medical devices, and digital health companies.
methodology: Tracked via iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB). Covers NASDAQ-listed biotech firms. Limitations: Excludes many medtech and digital health companies.
overview: Healthcare innovation is driven by demographic trends (aging populations), technological breakthroughs (gene therapy, mRNA), and regulatory approvals. Binary outcomes from drug trials create unique risk profiles.
risks: ⚖️ Regulatory Risk: FDA approvals/rejections create binary outcomes
📉 Clinical Trial Risk: Drug failures can cause significant losses
💰 Pricing Pressure: Political scrutiny of drug pricing
🔄 Patent Cliffs: Revenue drops when key patents expire
📊 High Volatility: Individual stock moves can be extreme
limitations: Excludes many medtech and digital health companies.
whoItsFor: You believe in long-term medical innovation
You can handle all-or-nothing drug trial results
You want diversification beyond tech
whoItsNotFor: You're investing for less than 5 years

name: Emerging Markets
description: Broad exposure to developing economies including China, India, Brazil, and others.
methodology: Tracked via iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (EEM). Broad diversified EM exposure. Limitations: China often >30% weight; may not represent all EM equally.
overview: Emerging market returns are driven by GDP growth differentials, commodity cycles, currency movements, and capital flows. They offer diversification but with additional political and currency risks.
risks: 🌍 Political Risk: Governance and policy instability in developing nations
💱 Currency Risk: Local currency depreciation erodes returns
📉 Capital Flow Risk: Vulnerable to sudden foreign capital withdrawal
⚖️ Regulatory Uncertainty: Changing rules can impact foreign investors
📊 Higher Volatility: Typically more volatile than developed market equities
limitations: China often >30% weight; may not represent all EM equally.
whoItsFor: You want global diversification
You believe developing economies will grow faster
You have a long time horizon (10+ years)

name: Dividend Income
description: High-dividend-yield stocks focused on consistent income generation.
methodology: Tracked via Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF (VYM). ~400+ stocks screened for above-average dividend yield. Limitations: Focuses on yield, not dividend growth.
overview: Dividend strategies focus on mature companies with stable cash flows. Returns come from both payments and moderate capital appreciation. They tend to underperform in strong growth markets but provide downside cushion.
risks: 📉 Interest Rate Sensitivity: Dividend stocks compete with bonds; rising rates reduce appeal
🔄 Dividend Cuts: Companies may reduce dividends during economic stress
🎯 Sector Concentration: Often heavy in utilities, financials, and real estate
💰 Growth Lag: May underperform growth-oriented strategies in bull markets
📊 Moderate Volatility: Generally lower than broad market but not immune
limitations: Focuses on yield, not dividend growth.
whoItsFor: You want regular income from your investments
You prefer larger, more stable companies
You're saving for retirement
whoItsNotFor: You don't need income right now

name: Inflation Protection
description: TIPS, commodities, and real assets designed to hedge against rising prices.
methodology: Tracked via iShares TIPS Bond ETF (TIP). US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities. Limitations: Pure TIPS exposure — does not include commodities or real estate.
overview: Inflation-protected strategies aim to preserve purchasing power. TIPS adjust principal with CPI. Returns are modest in low-inflation environments but provide insurance during inflationary periods.
risks: 📉 Low Real Returns: May underperform equities significantly over long periods
💰 Deflation Risk: TIPS can lose value in deflationary environments
🔄 Interest Rate Risk: Duration exposure means price declines when real rates rise
🎯 Limited Upside: Designed for protection, not wealth accumulation
📊 Low Volatility: Generally stable but with lower expected returns
limitations: Pure TIPS exposure — does not include commodities or real estate.
whoItsFor: You worry about rising prices eating into your savings
You want a calmer, more protective investment
You're looking to preserve wealth, not grow it fast
whoItsNotFor: You're young and can take more risk

name: Commodities
description: Broad commodity exposure including energy, metals, and agriculture.
methodology: Tracked via iPath Bloomberg Commodity Index ETN (DJP). Broad commodity futures basket. Limitations: Futures-based — subject to contango drag; ETN structure has credit risk.
overview: Commodity returns are driven by supply-demand dynamics, geopolitical events, weather, and inflation expectations. They often have low correlation with equities, providing diversification benefits.
risks: 📉 Contango Drag: Futures-based products may lose value from roll costs
🌍 Geopolitical Sensitivity: Prices heavily influenced by political events
🔄 Cyclicality: Commodity prices follow boom-bust super-cycles
💰 No Income: Commodities don't generate dividends or interest
📊 High Volatility: Individual commodity swings can be extreme
limitations: Futures-based — subject to contango drag; ETN structure has credit risk.
whoItsFor: You want something that doesn't move with stocks
You're worried about inflation
You want to diversify beyond traditional investments
whoItsNotFor: You want regular income or dividends
You can't tolerate sharp price swings

name: US Mega Cap Tech
description: Largest US technology companies by market capitalization.
methodology: Tracked via Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ). NASDAQ-100 index — top 100 non-financial NASDAQ stocks. Limitations: Not purely tech — includes consumer, healthcare, and telecom names.
overview: Mega cap tech returns are driven by digital advertising, cloud computing, consumer electronics, and platform economics. These companies have dominant market positions but face increasing regulatory scrutiny.
risks: 🎯 Concentration Risk: A few companies dominate index returns
⚖️ Antitrust Risk: Regulatory actions could force breakups or limit growth
📉 Valuation Risk: Premium valuations leave little margin for disappointment
🔄 Market Rotation: Growth-to-value rotations can cause sharp underperformance
📊 Moderate-High Volatility: Tech-heavy exposure amplifies market drawdowns
limitations: Not purely tech — includes consumer, healthcare, and telecom names.
whoItsFor: You want exposure to dominant technology platforms
You're comfortable with tech-heavy concentration
You're investing for 5+ years
whoItsNotFor: You worry about big tech regulation

name: Bitcoin / Digital Assets
description: Exposure to Bitcoin and the broader digital asset ecosystem.
methodology: Tracked via iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT). Spot Bitcoin ETF. Limitations: Launched Jan 2024 — limited history; uses BTC price for extended backtest.
overview: Bitcoin returns are driven by adoption trends, monetary policy expectations, regulatory developments, and speculative sentiment. It exhibits very high volatility and low correlation with traditional assets.
risks: 📊 Extreme Volatility: Drawdowns of 50-80% have occurred historically
⚖️ Regulatory Risk: Government bans or restrictions remain possible
🔄 Market Manipulation: Less regulated markets may be subject to manipulation
💰 No Intrinsic Cash Flow: Value based on supply scarcity and demand, not earnings
🌍 Custody/Security Risk: Unique risks around digital asset security
limitations: Launched Jan 2024 — limited history; uses BTC price for extended backtest.
whoItsFor: You can handle losing 50%+ and not panicking
You see Bitcoin as a long-term store of value
This would be a very small part of your portfolio
whoItsNotFor: You can't stomach seeing your money halve in value
